import re
import pytest
from target import unescapeHTML, _htmlentity_transform, compat_str


def expected_unescapeHTML(s):
    """Reference implementation using the old regex pattern."""
    if s is None:
        return None
    assert type(s) == compat_str
    return re.sub(r'&([^&;]+;)', lambda m: _htmlentity_transform(m.group(1)), s)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "input_str",
    [
        None,
        "",
        "plain text",
        "Hello & world",
        "<tag>",
        "Mix & < &unknown; &foo&bar; end",
        "Multiple &<> entities",
        "Edge &; case",
        "Invalid &foo&bar; entity",
        "Valid & then invalid &foo&bar; then <",
    ],
)
def test_unescapeHTML_behaviour_matches_old(input_str):
    """Ensure the new implementation behaves like the old one for various cases."""
    assert unescapeHTML(input_str) == expected_unescapeHTML(input_str)


def test_invalid_entity_with_amp_inside_is_unchanged():
    """Specific regression test: strings containing '&' inside an entity should remain unchanged."""
    s = "A &foo&bar; B"
    assert unescapeHTML(s) == expected_unescapeHTML(s)
    # Both should return the original string because the entity is malformed
    assert unescapeHTML(s) == s
    assert expected_unescapeHTML(s) == s


def test_valid_and_invalid_entities_mixed():
    """Mixed valid and malformed entities should only transform the valid ones."""
    s = "Start & middle &foo&bar; end <."
    expected = expected_unescapeHTML(s)
    result = unescapeHTML(s)
    assert result == expected
    # Ensure the malformed part is untouched
    assert "&foo&bar;" in result
    # Ensure the valid parts are transformed
    assert "&" not in result
    assert "<" not in result
